methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Mind Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by RJ Scaringe, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company. The peer set spans adjacent stages (Seed through Series B) within the robotics sector, including Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two valuation methods are applied. Stage-progression uses the company's $1.0B total capital raised as a proxy base, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $2.0B. Peer-median triangulation across five same-sector comparables (ranging from $1.1B to $2.0B, with a median of $1.6B) reflects market pricing for robotics companies at this stage and capitalization level. The peer-median method is constrained by the availability of late-stage robotics comps trading at higher valuations, which may compress the comparison.

The two methods triangulate to a range of $1.4B (floor) to $2.3B (ceiling), with a median implied valuation of $1.8B. This midpoint reflects the tension between stage-based growth expectations and observed peer pricing. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the public comp set (limited to one ticker) and whether the private peer cohort—skewed toward Series B—adequately captures Series A risk and dilution dynamics. Revenue traction and capital efficiency metrics would refine this range materially.
